items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: I’d send him right over to Snooky Young, and let’s sit down at the drums and play along with Snooky Young and show him how to phrase.

ctx.x: A couple of times the subject has come up about playing on top of the beat, playing behind the beat. Does such a thing exist?

Well if you play on the top you rush. If you play behind you drag. Now if the rhythm did that, if they laid back, they’d be dragging see? If the band goes, “Well we’re going to lay back.” “Well we’ll join you.” “Oh, no, no, no, it’ll slow down.” And everybody played right in tempo, like Count Basie does. Basie’s band, do they lay back? I says no they don’t. Play the records you can hear the rhythm drop out. They go swinging straight ahead. Basie never allowed that. He always had Sweets Edison, Buck Clayton and…
You’ve played on hundreds of records I would think.
